angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 317,935 km at 171.04 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.8466 +/- 0.0308 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 171.04 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.457 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Bernabò et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6383 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..273B/abstract): 317,935 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.458 +/- 0.011 solar masses from Bernabò et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6383 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..273B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3444 +/- 88 K from Bernabò et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6383 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..273B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bernabò et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6383 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..273B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6383-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.779, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
